request.report: Round 12: (1) Analyzed the completed off/greedy and A/greedy (ngram-mod defaults) replay results: A gives 86 tok/s single-agent (+56% vs off) but only ~neutral-to-slightly-worse dual fg (25.5 vs 26.3 agent, 23.8 vs 25.0 mem); draft acceptance collapses in dual to 14%/9.3% vs 75.5% single-agent. (2) Confirmed the mmproj+spec verdict empirically: all runs report 9507 MiB VRAM, no -nommproj fallback, no checkpoint-mode refusal, draft_n>0 and draft_n_accepted>0 for both agent and mem → ngram-mod runs with --mmproj on text-only traffic. (3) Found at temp 0 the outputs are NOT identical between arms (fg out_sha256: single-agent 3/30, single-mem 10/12, dual-agent 10/38, dual-mem 11/19 identical) — must investigate before deploy. (4) Recorded all of this in bench/m1-notes.md §9 (results) and §10 (B choice). B = ngram-mod with --spec-ngram-mod-n-max 128 (double the default draft size), which matches the script's hard-coded B label; justified as the cleanest axis-isolating probe on the proven algorithm.
request.why: Run the required next phase (B/greedy) in the off → A → B → prod order. It needs the GPU via turnstile (llama-server on private :8089) and spins up a fresh server per phase, so it must run on the GPU slot. Completing B lets me pick the best of A/B for the final off/prod and best/prod runs.
